hints: Notice the axes are force in $\text{N}$ up to $250$ and extension in $\text{mm}$ up to $10$, and work done is the total area under the curve to breaking.
Notice the shape has two parts: a steep elastic line to $200 \text{ N}$ at about $1 \text{ mm}$, then a shallow plastic line to $250 \text{ N}$ at $10 \text{ mm}$.
Convert $\text{mm}$ to $\text{m}$ and add the small triangle plus the trapezium with average force about $225 \text{ N}$ over about $9 \text{ mm}$.
walkthrough: Work done to stretch the wire is the area under the force-extension graph, $W = \text{area under } F \text{ against } x$, up to the breaking extension of $10 \text{ mm} = 0.010 \text{ m}$.
Split the area into two simple shapes. First is the steep elastic triangle from $0$ to about $1 \text{ mm}$ with peak $200 \text{ N}$: $W_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 200 \times 0.001 = 0.10 \text{ J}$.
Second is the long shallow section from about $1 \text{ mm}$ to $10 \text{ mm}$, which is a trapezium between $200 \text{ N}$ and $250 \text{ N}$ over $\Delta x = 9 \text{ mm} = 0.009 \text{ m}$.
Its area is average force times extension: $W_2 = \frac{200+250}{2} \times 0.009 = 225 \times 0.009 = 2.025 \text{ J}$.
Total work is $W = W_1 + W_2 \approx 0.10 + 2.025 = 2.125 \text{ J}$, so the best estimate is about $2.1 \text{ J}$. This is option A.
